PPTI Research Publication Trends and Strategic Positioning

A bibliometric report on recent PPTI publication activity, journal distribution, citation visibility, open-access status, and research themes.

Nov 1, 2026, 3:25 AM UTC

Abstract

This report examines 570Source for 570Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications distinct Scopus-indexed publications associated with 64Source for 64Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications PPTI researchers during the 24Source for 24Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications-month period from 1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications November 2024 to 31Source for 31Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications October 2026. The publications appeared in 315Source for 315Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications journals and had received 2,647Source for 2,647Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications citations at the time of data collection. The analysis considers publication activity, journal concentration, citation visibility, open-access status, and recurring author keywords to describe the institution's recent research profile. The results show a broad journal portfolio, with the ten most frequently used titles accounting for 21%Source for 21%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications. Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization was the most frequently used journal, with 21Source for 21Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications articles, while Fermentation was the most prevalent normalized author keyword, appearing in 14Source for 14Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications publications. Open-access articles represented 44%Source for 44%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of the portfolio. Journals below the established tier accounted for 72%Source for 72%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications, while developing and exploratory keywords accounted for 88%Source for 88%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publication–keyword associations. Compared with the September 2026 edition, the rolling portfolio contained 11 more distinct publications; its cumulative citation total was 104Source for 104Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications higher and the open-access share moved +0.8Source for +0.8Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications percentage points. Together, these findings provide an evidence base for understanding PPTI's publication patterns and for aligning future manuscripts with demonstrated areas of research activity and journal experience.

1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications. Scope and method

The report is based on Scopus publication records associated with PPTI researchers and dated between 1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications November 2024 to 31Source for 31Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications October 2026. The unit of analysis is a distinct Scopus-indexed publication rather than an author–publication record; consequently, a publication co-authored by more than one PPTI researcher is counted once in the portfolio totals. Citation values represent the cumulative Scopus counts available when the dataset was collected, and thematic analysis is based on normalized author keywords. Monthly commentary is generated by comparing the current metrics and rankings with the preceding saved edition under the same methodology. Journal and keyword frequencies therefore describe both the present portfolio and any material movement since the previous report.

Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization became the leading journal, with 21Source for 21Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications distinct publications; the previous leader, International Journal of Biological Macromolecules, ranked 1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications. 3.3Source for 3.3Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications Publication frequency and citation visibility

The journal map relates the number of distinct publications in each outlet to their cumulative citation totals. Journals positioned toward the upper right combine repeated PPTI publication activity with comparatively strong citation visibility. In contrast, a journal with high citation counts but few publications may reflect the influence of a small number of articles. The two measures are therefore presented as complementary dimensions of the portfolio: frequency indicates the extent of recent use, whereas citations indicate the visibility accumulated by the articles published in that outlet.

5Source for 5Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications. Conclusion

PPTI's recent Scopus-indexed output is characterized by sustained publication activity, a broad journal base, and identifiable concentrations of research expertise. Across 570Source for 570Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications distinct publications, the portfolio combines repeated use of established outlets with dissemination across 315Source for 315Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications journals, while 44%Source for 44%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of articles were available through open access. The tier analysis shows that 72%Source for 72%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications occurred in developing or exploratory journals and that 88%Source for 88%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publication–keyword associations sat outside the established keyword tier. Compared with the September 2026 edition, the rolling portfolio contained 11 more distinct publications; its cumulative citation total was 104Source for 104Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications higher and the open-access share moved +0.8Source for +0.8Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications percentage points. The journal and keyword results together document the institution's recent publication position and provide a reproducible baseline against which subsequent reporting periods can be compared.
